title: the words this door is written in
description: What a content file's frontmatter SAYS (T-34606, T-34649): public/guide/<slug>.md is a `guide`, prompts/<name>.md is a `prompt`, and each names its entity by its own identity column rather than by an eid somebody wrote down. Loading a file twice is one entity — the id is derived from the value (@yaks/graph identity.ts) — which is why the frontmatter carries no `entity` line at all. gen.ts reads these files into content.ts; nothing applies them to a store yet, and this is the vocabulary the day something does.

guide.description: A page of the guide, offered through the connector as a resource of its own.

slug.description: The page's name, in its address and in its file's: public/guide/<slug>.md. It IS the page — gen.ts refuses a file whose frontmatter and filename disagree.

brief.description: A few words, for the `guide` tool's own description, which names every page at once.

description.description: The sentence an agent reads before deciding to read the page — the only thing it sees first.

prompt.description: A thing a person picks by name: a slash command, a menu entry. The message itself is the file's body, and its `arguments` are the file's own word — a list is not a column, so a store holds the row and the file holds the slots.

name.description: What a client calls it, in its file's name: prompts/<name>.md.

title.description: What a person reads on the menu.

description.description: What the prompt is for, as the client lists it.
